title: Classic Gosaikunda Trek (shortest option)
route_chain_display: Dhunche ↔ Gosaikunda ↔ Dhunche
highlights: Sacred lakes, alpine scenery, Tamang culture.
overview: Gosaikunda Lake, located at an altitude of 4,380 meters in the Langtang region of Nepal, is a sacred alpine lake revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. Surrounded by rugged hills and snow-capped peaks, the lake is believed to have been created by Lord Shiva with his trident to quench his thirst after swallowing poison. It’s the centerpiece of the Gosaikunda trek, which passes through Langtang National Park and offers stunning views of the Himalayas, including Langtang Lirung and Ganesh Himal. During the Janai Purnima festival, thousands of pilgrims make a spiritual journey to its pristine waters, making it both a scenic and culturally rich destination.

overview: Mardi Himal Base Camp, situated at around 4,500 meters, is a hidden gem in the Annapurna region of Nepal. This short yet scenic trek offers spectacular close-up views of Mardi Himal, Machapuchare (Fishtail), and the Annapurna range. Less crowded than other treks, it leads you through rhododendron forests, ridge trails, and high alpine landscapes. The base camp offers a peaceful setting with dramatic mountain backdrops, making it a perfect off-the-beaten-path adventure for nature lovers and photographers alike.

title: Manaslu Circuit Trek (Classic Route)

overview: Manaslu Base Camp, located at approximately 4,800 meters above sea level, sits below Mount Manaslu (8,163 m), the world’s 8th highest mountain. This lesser-known trekking route offers a peaceful alternative to the crowded trails of Everest and Annapurna. The journey passes through the culturally rich Nubri and Tsum valleys, showcasing Tibetan-influenced villages, ancient monasteries, and lush forests. The base camp itself offers jaw-dropping views of Manaslu's towering icy slopes and surrounding peaks, all within the serene setting of the Manaslu Conservation Area.

overview: Everest Base Camp (EBC), located at an altitude of 5,364 meters, is the gateway to the world’s highest peak—Mount Everest (8,848.86 m). The trek to EBC is one of the most iconic journeys on Earth, offering dramatic mountain views, Sherpa culture, and historic landmarks like the Tengboche Monastery. Along the way, trekkers pass through Sagarmatha National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site rich in Himalayan wildlife. EBC is not just about reaching the base—it’s about the adventure through Khumbu Valley, standing face to face with giants like Lhotse, Nuptse, and Everest itself

title: Classic Shey Phoksundo Lake Trek (Most Popular)
route_chain_display: Kathmandu ✈️Juphal → Shey Phoksundo Lake → Juphal
highlights: The turquoise Shey Phoksundo Lake •The Phoksundo Waterfall (167 m) — Nepal’s highest waterfall •Tibetan-style Ringmo Village with Bonpo monasteries •Inside Shey Phoksundo National Park (home to snow leopards, blue sheep) •Moderate altitude and accessible for most trekkers
overview: Shey Phoksundo Lake, nestled at 3,611 m in Nepal’s remote Dolpa region, is the country’s deepest (145 m) and second-largest alpine lake, known for its surreal turquoise waters and rugged surroundings . It was formed by an ancient glacial landslide dam and is home to the majestic Phoksundo Waterfall, the highest free-falling waterfall in Nepal at about 167 m . The lake sits within Shey Phoksundo National Park—Nepal’s largest trans-Himalayan park, rich in biodiversity with snow leopards, musk deer, blue sheep, red pandas, and over 200 bird species . Cultural serenity reigns in nearby Ringmo village, where Tibetan-Bon traditions thrive and century‑old gompas and stupas dot the lake’s shores.

overview: Shey Phoksundo Lake, nestled at 3,611 m in Nepal’s remote Dolpa region, is the country’s deepest (145 m) and second-largest alpine lake, known for its surreal turquoise waters and rugged surroundings . It was formed by an ancient glacial landslide dam and is home to the majestic Phoksundo Waterfall, the highest free-falling waterfall in Nepal at about 167 m . The lake sits within Shey Phoksundo National Park—Nepal’s largest trans-Himalayan park, rich in biodiversity with snow leopards, musk deer, blue sheep, red pandas, and over 200 bird species . Cultural serenity reigns in nearby Ringmo village, where Tibetan-Bon traditions thrive and century‑old gompas and stupas dot the lake’s shores.

overview: Makalu Base Camp sits at an altitude of around 4,870 meters in eastern Nepal and offers a remote and adventurous trekking experience. highlights: North Annapurna Base Camp
overview: Annapurna Base Camp (ABC), nestled at an altitude of 4,130 meters in central Nepal, is a breathtaking natural amphitheater surrounded by some of the world’s highest peaks. The area is also part of the Annapurna Conservation Area. Nepal’s first and largest conservation region, rich in biodiversity and home to rare wildlife like snow leopards and red pandas. Uniquely, the base camp lies in the heart of a massive glacier basin, offering 360-degree panorama of snowcapped giants that glow golden at sunrise making it one of the most photogenic trekking destinations in the world.
